conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Officer Daniel Harper speaking. This call is regarding your federal income taxes. Can you confirm your full name for the record, please?
Um, yes, hi, my name is Jamie Collins. I got a message saying there was some kind of urgent tax situation?

Thank you, Ms. Collins. For verification, I am badge number 215478-B under the IRS collections division. According to our system, there are discrepancies in your tax filings for the past two years resulting in a significant outstanding liability.
I'm really confused. I just graduated last year, do I really owe taxes? I thought I did everything right with my part-time job...

The matter is quite serious. The IRS has conducted an audit using Form 1040 records linked to your Social Security number. It appears you underreported income, resulting in tax deficiencies, accrued interest, and failure-to-pay penalties.
Oh my God. I had no idea. How much am I supposed to owe? I really don't have any money right now.

At this time, your total assessed liability is $3,178.22, including late payment fees and federal penalties. If this balance is not resolved within 48 hours, we are required by statute 26 U.S. Code § 6331 to initiate a levy on your bank accounts and a federal lien against your assets.
Wait, what does that mean? I barely have $100 in my checking account. Will I go to jail or something?

Ms. Collins, failure to comply leaves you exposed to criminal prosecution for tax evasion under 26 U.S. Code § 7201. This could lead to freezing your accounts, wage garnishment, or referral to federal law enforcement for immediate arrest.
Please, I can't, I'm already behind on my student loans. Is there any way to stop this? I don't know what to do.

The IRS can offer you a one-time settlement program to avoid legal escalation. However, you must demonstrate intent to resolve the outstanding taxes right now. Would you like to proceed under the expedited compliance protocol?
Yes, please. I don't want any trouble. What do I need to do?

To begin, you must make an initial settlement payment of at least $1,500 today. The IRS accepts electronic payments via wire transfer, cryptocurrency, or IRS-approved prepaid debit cards. Which method is available to you right now?
I, um, I don't have any crypto. I have a debit card, but there's not enough. What is a prepaid card for the IRS? I don't understand.

Prepaid cards are IRS-authorized vouchers you can purchase at major retailers such as Walmart, CVS, or Walgreens. Once obtained, you will provide the codes to me for immediate processing to halt enforcement actions.
Are you sure this is real? I've never heard of paying taxes this way before.

Ms. Collins, do not interfere with federal procedures. This is a confidential compliance process. Non-payment will result in an immediate case referral to the Department of Justice, and you could be subject to arrest within hours. Do you wish to cooperate or escalate this matter?
No, no, I'll do it. I just don't want to get in trouble. So I just go to the store and buy the cards?
Correct. Purchase $1,500 worth of Apple or Target gift cards. Remain on the line while you do this. Once you have the cards, read me the codes on the back for IRS validation.
Okay... I'll need to go out now. Please don't call the police or anything. I'm going now.
Stay on the call at all times. If the call disconnects or you delay, your file will be flagged for immediate enforcement. Notify me as soon as you reach the store.
